version_policy: The inner Requirements packet remains unversioned. No second packet shape, version alias or mutation fallback is introduced. Explicit migration settings use schema requirements-sql-1; unknown keys are ignored, missing required known keys and unsupported schema values refuse.

standalone_denial.reason: Запись требований требует действующей Task. Передайте этот пакет как work.operation=requirements через poise runtime --settings "$runtime_settings", указав существующий файл настроек runtime.

types.packet: Exactly operation:string and input:object. No nullable or omitted input. Existing business command/apply/query/import_bootstrap shapes and business/replay results remain their existing contracts inside the owned operation.
types.status: Exactly action=status; result revision is a nonnegative signed SQLite INTEGER, state is 64 lowercase hexadecimal SHA256 digits, applied and pending are sorted distinct migration-ID string arrays. applied observes ordinary global library status; pending contains current Task migration files only. This public result supplies apply/rollback guards.
types.apply_rollback: All four fields required, no null. action is apply or rollback. migration_ids is a nonempty array of nonempty distinct string IDs, each naming a real current Task SQL pair. Input array order does not override the stock tool dependency order. expected_revision is a nonnegative signed SQLite INTEGER, expected_state is the status SHA256 string. Response IDs are actually changed identities in execution order.
types.export: All seven fields required, no null. request_id is a nonempty string with the existing Requirements request-ID constraints. source,target,output_directory are explicit absolute filesystem paths as strings. source and target are existing supported read-only snapshot/comparison inputs; neither is auto-created or initialized, and no library bookkeeping is created by export. target may differ from the configured mutable store. mode is full or selected. requirement_ids is an explicit empty array for full and a nonempty distinct requirement-ID string array for selected; no omitted all-mode default. No implicit source or destination.
types.settings: schema,schema_directory,data_directory,initial_directory are required strings. schema_directory and data_directory are distinct non-overlapping explicit repository-relative paths owned by the actual current Task and allowed stage. Their publication location authoritatively declares the source role, never SQL parsing, filename spelling, metadata sidecars or an applied-state ledger. initial_directory explicitly selects packaged immutable initial SQL. No task_directory alias or hidden fallback, and no caller-supplied Task, branch or worktree identity. Load both role sources together through the standard tool; dependency order remains authoritative across directories. Duplicate IDs or ambiguous/unclassified sources refuse. Squash only owned data sources; retain schema sources unchanged. A source role is not a general SQL semantic validator.

state_guard: SHA256 of UTF-8 canonical JSON described by contract.json state_contract. Only schema version, seven explicitly named business tables, revision and request receipt rows participate. Sorted row order is explicit there. Ordinary library bookkeeping/log rows are excluded. This is an optimistic guard, not a persisted second ledger. Verify it again at the actual mutation boundary.
repetition: With fresh matching guards, applying an already applied pair or rolling back an already unapplied pair succeeds with an empty affected-ID array and executes no SQL. A successful rollback permits a real later apply. Stale guards refuse even if the requested IDs would otherwise be no-op. No request ledger or permanent exactly-once rule is added for library actions. Business request replay remains the existing receipt contract; unresolved post-body bookkeeping is explicit manual recovery.
ownership: WorkTools uses the actual bound actor/Task, active allowed stage, actual configured branch/worktree and explicit supported configuration. Export output must equal the configured current Task data_directory. Ordinary data mutations publish there; historical schema migrations publish in schema_directory. Comparison target may differ from the configured mutable store. Export leaves source, comparison target and configured store unchanged, including schema/library bookkeeping; it never changes config/profile or redirects mutation. Actual apply/rollback uses only its configured mutable store and revalidates the captured target state there. A mismatch refuses without adapting literals or mutating the comparison input; explicit later target/config adoption belongs to its separate authorized owner. Missing comparison input, wrong output/Task/branch or tracked mutable store refuses before publication or business writes.
collisions: Reuse an existing complete output pair only for identical captured request and exact bytes. Changed intent, conflicting bytes, partial pair or different existing target row refuses. Identical dependencies are reused. Selected closure includes parent System, Application links and referenced domains/entities/actions; absent required source dependencies refuse. Full mode requires an empty target and preserves full source history/revision. Selected mode retains target history and issues its own receipt/revision. No changes emits no empty pair.
errors: Standalone denials use exit 2 and exactly standalone_denial. Owned contract/domain/SQL failures use the existing PoiseError boundary and native outer rejection transport, never a successful business response. SQL-body errors leave pre-body business/schema/revision/receipts and applied status. Post-committed-body bookkeeping errors explicitly identify manual standard-tool status repair and the known committed/uncertain boundary; retry cannot falsely report normal success. No second error transport.

standalone_evolution.read: Existing standalone operation=query remains byte-for-byte business compatible and read-only.
standalone_evolution.breaking_change: The new work operation is additive, but blocking these old standalone writes is an explicit breaking semantic change. Their owned inner packet shapes remain supported; there is no compatibility write bypass.
producers_consumers: Native standalone Requirements CLI and its maintained mutation tests/fixtures
Native WorkTools/runtime adapter producer and Requirements application mutation owners
Native agent/operator initialization, bootstrap and historical schema migration instructions
ERP task-management req-ctl/workflow_proxy.py Requirements transport and agent consumers: separately migrate and verify in parent ERP Task; native tests do not establish ERP adoption
